passage:
Some students were afraid to ask questions in class. They worried their questions were silly.
The teacher placed a question box near the door. Students could write questions on paper and put them inside. Every Friday, the teacher answered several.
The questions were useful. Some showed that many students did not understand the same idea. Others were interesting and led to new discussions.
One question said, "Why do we need to learn this" The teacher answered seriously and explained where the lesson could be used.
The box helped students speak without fear. It also helped the teacher see what silence had hidden.
A quiet classroom is not always a classroom with no questions.
